what_this_is: two more operators tested (semantic backpropagation and a matched-difficulty decoy), and the observation that redirects the line: every operator fails at the same rung

the_identity_that_motivated_it.derivation: out = A + B*v, and the forward pass yields v and out, so v* = v + (want - out)/B
the_identity_that_motivated_it.verified: 24303 of 24303 (address, point) pairs with B != 0: splicing v* makes the tree exact
the_identity_that_motivated_it.note: B == 0 marks points the address cannot affect, so there is no requirement to meet there -- genuine don't-cares and extra freedom, not missing data

first_attempt_failed_for_a_measurable_re.design: require an EXACT match of the required vector on every constrained point
first_attempt_failed_for_a_measurable_re.splice_failures: 23991 of about 24000 attempts, a 99.96% failure rate
first_attempt_failed_for_a_measurable_re.cause: a required vector is twelve arbitrary rationals and essentially no library subtree produces exactly that, so the arm degenerated to mutation-only through its own fallback while spending 26x the evaluations
first_attempt_failed_for_a_measurable_re.fix: nearest match instead of exact. Exactness was never needed for soundness, since the Lean kernel still decides acceptance, so the splice is free to be a heuristic

and_my_control_was_broken.defect: the decoy target was drawn FROM THE LIBRARY, making it matchable by construction: 200 failures against the treatment's 23991
and_my_control_was_broken.why_it_mattered: the control was easier than its treatment for a reason unrelated to the hypothesis, so it measured difficulty rather than correctness
and_my_control_was_broken.fix: the decoy is now fresh random rationals, so both arms face the same matching problem

the_metric_artifact: At L3 semantic backpropagation reaches a solution in a median 388.5 fitness evaluations against mutation-only's 1203 -- a 3.1x win in the budgeted currency. Its tree-point cost is 478434 against 24834, which is 19x. Reporting the 3.1x alone would be true and thoroughly misleading: the operator spends its savings about six times over in probe cost it does not charge itself. This is why both metrics are reported for every arm.
the_finding_that_redirects_the_line: EIGHT operators have now been tested -- mutation, random crossover, homologous, anti-homologous, contribution-preserving, same-sites-unscaled, semantic backpropagation, and its matched decoy -- and ALL of them collapse between L3 (size 9, solve rates around 0.3-0.6) and L4 (size 11, at most 1 of 12). A cliff that every variation mechanism hits in the same place is not a property of any operator. The bottleneck is the landscape or the representation, not the variation mechanism, and further operator design is the wrong place to spend effort.
why_a_200_seed_run_was_not_done: The decisive observations do not need power: both semantic arms are 0 of 12 at L4 and L5 where mutation manages 1 of 12, and the efficiency claim is refuted by its own cost column rather than by a p-value. Scaling to 200 seeds would refine a null.
not_established: 12 seeds, so the L3 differences (7 vs 6 vs 5) are noise and are not interpreted.
One library size (16 sampled subtrees plus 7 terminals) and at most 3 probed addresses. A larger library might match better, at proportionally more cost in the column that already shows 19x.

The cliff's CAUSE is not established here, only its operator-independence. L4 requires assembling a three-factor product with no partial credit, which is a plausible deceptive landscape, but that is a hypothesis and not a measurement.
